summary: DHCPv6 temporary lease collision prevents corp certificate auto-rotation on repaired laptops
description:
Issue summary:
Several devices coming back from depot repair fail automated corporate certificate rotation during first post-repair checkin. Failure correlates with DHCPv6 temporary address collisions at the repair facility network; the provisioning agent attempts rotation but receives an identical IPv6 temporary address (TLA/ULA conflict) already mapped to a different device, causing the cert-rotation handshake to stall and the agent to retry into exponential backoff.

Impact:
- A subset (~6%) of repaired laptops are blocked from rotating machine certificates on first checkin, delaying MDM enrollment and blocking policy application.
- Affects devices reprovisioned from depot repair facility in us-east region.
- No user-facing data loss, but devices remain in partial-managed state for up to 24+ hours unless manually remediated.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east) depot repair VLAN (172.31.200.0/24) with IPv6 SLAAC + stateful DHCPv6 enabled on site router appliance.
- Devices: Dell Precision 5570 and Lenovo ThinkPad T14 generations returned for keyboard replacement.
- Provisioning stack: intune-agent v4.3.1 -> provisioning-agent v2.8.0 -> cert-rotation service (internal)

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Device receives temporary IPv6 address via router's SLAAC/DHCPv6 on depot repair VLAN.
2) Device runs provisioning-agent first-boot flow and requests corp machine cert via cert-rotation endpoint.
3) Cert-rotation performs IP/hostname correlation checks; backend ledger shows a different device already holding a lease with same IPv6 temporary address (collision).
4) Agent stalls waiting for ephemeral confirmation, retries with backoff, and eventually reports failure to CS.

Observed behavior:
- provisioning-agent logs show repeated "ip_conflict_detected: temporary_ipv6 already in ledger" followed by exponential-retry and eventual "certificate rotation timed out".
- Affected devices get flagged as "partial-managed" in console and show missing machine certs.

Expected behavior:
- Cert rotation should tolerate transient temporary IPv6 collisions at depot networks by falling back to alternative identifier (MAC/serial) or forcing short randomized client ID for rotation handshake.
steps_to_reproduce: Ship device to depot facility and boot on depot VLAN
Allow SLAAC/DHCPv6 to assign temporary IPv6 address
Observe provisioning-agent attempting first checkin and cert rotation
Check cert-rotation logs for ip_conflict_detected entries
logs: 2026-03-09T08:15:50Z provisioning-agent[pid=2145]: rotation_fail: timeout after retries; error=certificate rotation timed out
investigation_notes: Confirmed increased collision events on depot VLAN via dhcpv6-snoop logs between 2026-03-08 and 2026-03-09.
Ledger currently keys cert requests by IP+clientid; collisions occur when temporary IPv6 addresses are non-unique across NAT/proxy segments at repair facility.
Reproduced locally by spinning up two VMs on same depot VLAN emulator and forcing identical temporary IPv6 (SLAAC edge case); provisioning-agent blocked as seen in field.
Checked related tickets: INT-660321 (networkmanager duplicate route) and INT-272831 (kmod-signature); networking team aware of odd VLAN config at depot vendor.
No changes to provisioning-agent code between baseline good fleet and failing cohort; likely environmental IPv6 lease footprint at repair site.
hypothesis: Repair facility network is performing IPv6 address recycling or proxying in a way that causes identical temporary SLAAC/DHCPv6 addresses to appear for multiple devices. The cert-rotation service's strict IP-based correlation is not tolerant to transient collisions.
temporary_workaround:
1) On inbound repair returns, instruct depot to isolate devices into per-device VLANs (short-term).
2) Manually trigger provisioning-agent restart with --force-clientid flag to use serial-based client id for cert rotation (run by support).
3) Added short-lived server-side mitigation: mark collision events as transient and accept rotation if serial/MAC matches within 30s window (hotfix toggled on 2026-03-12).
resolution: Mitigation applied: backend hotfix tolerates transient ip collisions for 30s window when serial or MAC correlates, and support documented a depot isolation playbook. Engineering roadmap item opened to make client rotate by default to serial-based handshake as a durable fix.
comments: Ava Patel (2026-03-10): Initial report from Depot Ops — ~12 devices failed cert rotation after keyboard replacement batch.
Marcus Chen (2026-03-11): I reproduced a collision in the lab by forcing identical temporary IPv6 via emulator; starting analysis of ledger logic.
SRE (Liam O'Connor) (2026-03-12): Deployed temporary backend toggle to accept serial match within 30s window as a mitigation; monitoring for false positives.
Depot Ops (Maya Ruiz) (2026-03-12): We will isolate repairs into ephemeral VLANs today and escalate if more failures seen.
Marcus Chen (2026-03-13): Hotfix in place; marking this ticket In Progress until we complete durable change in provisioning-agent.
slo_impact: No external customer SLA. Internal reprovisioning delay window increased from target <2h to observed 6-24h for affected devices.
next_steps: Ship provisioning-agent change to default to serial-based client id for rotation (Engineering) - PR #789
Coordinate with Depot vendor to reconfigure IPv6 handling and ensure per-device isolation (Ops)
Monitor production depot VLAN for 72h for recurrence and collect dhcpv6-snoop traces on each failure (SRE)
